page: Amazon Web Services t3.nano is an entry-level, burstable compute instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz, provisioned as two virtual CPUs across one physical core with hyperthreading enabled. Memory capacity is restricted to 0.5 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz (0.25 GB per vCPU). The instance includes no integrated local storage and features a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps, meaning network performance relies on standard burst allocations.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within the lowest tiers across compute and throughput tests. In stress-ng evaluations, it achieved 1141.78 in single-core performance (bottom 25%) and 1661.39 in multi-core performance (bottom 10%). PassMark evaluations returned an overall CPU score of 1909.42, with extended instruction scores of 1412.52 and encryption at 762.8. Redis SET operations measured 1.5 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 1.72 GB/sec, reflecting the constrained resource envelope.

Given its minimal memory footprint and shared burstable CPU credits, the t3.nano offers high cost efficiency for low-duty background processes, lightweight automation scripts, monitoring agents, or basic development endpoints. It is unsuited for memory-intensive applications, persistent high-throughput workloads, or data processing pipelines due to strict RAM constraints and burst-dependent performance.
